heading: Explanations fitting a neuron's activating examples can mispredict its firing, so inspection overstates understanding
definition: an explanation that fits a neuron's activating examples can still fail to predict where it fires, so "one main job" by inspection overstates how much is explained.
summary: Independent groups find such mispredictions in GPT-2, Gemma 2, Llama 3.1 and several vision models, and how large the failure is depends on layer and explanation method. Only the original essay tests whether 'one main job' judgments made by inspection overstate what is explained, and it found failures for a minority of the Qwen3-32B neurons it tested.

suggested_status.by_scale: toy: theory/metric tests on idealized neurons only (2506.05774). <1B: R2 (counts versions.V6.studies_by_size['<1B'] = 3; small GPT-2 models in 2410.16443, a six-layer SoLU model in 2304.12918/2305.19911, Pythia-70M in 2309.08600). 1-10B: R2 (studies_by_size['1-10B'] = 6; GPT-2 XL in 2309.10312 and 2506.15538, Gemma 2 and Llama 3.1 in 2410.13928, 2502.12483 and 2502.16994). 10-100B: R0 (studies_by_size['10-100B'] = 1; only the essay's own Qwen3-32B test, which reports failure for a minority of neurons). >100B: nothing (no key in counts). Size not stated (studies_by_size['not stated'] = 17, mostly vision models): R2 across several groups (2405.20331, 2603.24953, 2506.07985, 2007.01062).
suggested_status.reason: The version's first clause, that explanations built from activating examples can fail to predict firing, is reproduced by groups other than the originals. Counts (counts.json was built before the checks and has not been rerun): versions.V6.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original = 0; verdicts.supports.studies = 24; verdicts.limits_scope.studies = 12; verdicts.challenges.studies = 0. The limits_scope tally still counts two verdicts that the checks overturned to supports, so it overstates the limits side until the counts are rerun. One is 2309.10312's verdict on form-based (spelling or regex-checkable) explanations. Form-based explanations have precision 0.78, against 0.62 for the rest, so false positives occur in both groups, and recall is not split by explanation type (2309.10312#r6, #r7). The other is 2506.07985's verdict on the ResNet-50 human ratings. The study names LE as its only full-range method, and LE stays above DnD: 0.1216 vs 0.0978 (majority vote) and 0.1261 vs 0.1011 (BRAgg uniform prior; LE>DnD p=0.0198) (2506.07985#r31, #r36). Both studies also have a supports verdict on V6 in the pack, so verdicts.supports.studies already includes them. The checks overturned no other V6 verdict and no V6 challenge, so the supports and challenges tallies quoted here are not affected. The first clause holds on several language-model families: GPT-2 XL (2309.10312: precision 0.64, recall 0.50) and Gemma 2 / Llama 3.1 (2410.13928: medians 0.53–0.62 vs 0.51 random; 2502.12483: IS 0.18 and 0.13). It also holds in vision models (2405.20331 MILAN; 2603.24953 Activation Rate 45–58%). How large the failure is depends on layer (N2G layer 0 vs layers 3–5 in 2304.12918), on explanation method (CLIP-Dissect vs MILAN in 2405.20331) and on how descriptions are selected. The second clause, that 'one main job' judged by inspection overstates how much is explained, is not tested directly by anyone other than the essay. At Qwen3-32B the essay finds failure for a minority: 164 of 183 explanations beat their near misses.
suggested_status.open_questions: (1) An independent test of audit-style explanations on Qwen3-32B or another model of 10–100B or more, scoring both precision (new and near-miss examples) and recall on natural text. If it reproduced the essay's 76% vs 11% result, the overstatement clause would fail at that scale (toward C there). If it found failures like those in GPT-2 XL, the clause would reach R2. (2) A per-neuron comparison of 'one main job' judgements with held-out prediction scores. (3) Any test above 100B or on MoE models. (4) Whether the two N2G papers and the two InceptionV1 human studies come from the same authors, which bears on how independent the replications are.

original_result.setup: For each of 183 Qwen3-32B neurons from the essay's gallery of examples, an AI agent saw only the neuron's explanation and wrote 5 texts that should fire the neuron and 5 near misses that should not.
original_result.result: 76% of the new examples fired their neuron strongly (at least 30% of its activation on its strongest corpus example), against 11% of near misses. Neuron by neuron, the explanation's examples beat its near misses for 164 neurons, tied for 15 and lost for 4.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: Treated as detectors of their top-image label, CNN units had high precision but very low recall.
Neuron-to-Graph token graphs built from top-activating examples mispredicted held-out firings in SoLU layers 1–5.
Scoring explanations only on top-activating inputs never penalized over-generic labels.
Two Whisper tiny neurons looked like single-phoneme units but were polysemantic at lower activations.
Images generated from inferred concepts reached the neuron's top-1% activation level only 45–58% of the time.
Excerpt-based explanations of one hard GPT-2 XL neuron predicted its activations poorly.
MILAN descriptions, written from top-activating image regions, barely predicted firing in most of six vision models.
BERT neuron patterns from one dataset's top sentences did not hold on other datasets.
Seeing top-activating images barely helped humans predict how hiding image patches changed InceptionV1 unit activations.
For higher-level concepts, descriptions fitting top-0.1% images failed on top-1% and top-5% images.
With synthetic or single natural reference images, humans told maximal from minimal activations only 64–82% correctly.
Explanations from top-activating fragments predicted Pythia-70M activations significantly worse on random text than on top-plus-random text.
Neuron-to-Graph (N2G) token graphs from top-activating examples mispredicted many held-out firings in SoLU layers 3–5.
High-scoring GPT-4 explanations of GPT-2 XL neurons still mispredicted firing on new sentences.
Explanations of Gemma 2 and Llama 3.1 neurons scored barely above random on held-out examples.
One GPT2-small neuron had a rare secondary behaviour the authors say top-example inspection would miss.
GPT-2 neuron explanations from top activations scored about half as well on random as top-plus-random text.
Explanations from top-3 activating examples predicted new neuron activations poorly.
Descriptions that scored well at simulating Llama-3.1-8B neurons still missed many inputs the neurons fired on.
Top-activation explanations correlated weakly with vision neuron activity across the full ImageNet validation set.
Single-cluster descriptions often failed to make GPT-2 XL and Llama neurons fire on new text.
Descriptions of Qwen2.5-based MLP neurons told activating from non-activating new snippets with only 0.80 accuracy.
GPT-5.4 predicted held-out OpenCLIP neuron activators well above chance but missed about 30%.

sources.source_id: TITLE:Language models can explain neurons in language models
sources.headline: Many sentences matching GPT-4 explanations of GPT-2 neurons failed to make them fire.
In layer 0, N2G token graphs predicted held-out firings fairly well.
CLIP-Dissect, a labelling method also built from top images, predicted firing well (AUC 0.78–0.95).
In a coarser two-image task, natural reference images gave 84% accuracy versus 65% for synthetic ones.
Low-level concepts like colours held more consistently in the top 1% and 5% images.
With nine max- and nine min-activating natural references, humans told maximal from minimal activations 91–92% correctly.
N2G token graphs captured early SoLU layers fairly well, so failure depends on depth.
Explanations about surface form, like spelling, predicted firing with higher precision (0.78) than other explanations.
From top-plus-random to random text, explanation scores held in one-layer models and dipped in interpretable-by-design CRATE.
Prompt-tuned top-activation descriptions (MaxAct*) matched firing moderately well, so failure size depended on method and layer.
DnD matched CLIP-Dissect on ResNet-50 human ratings but stayed below LE.
Each neuron's best of five PRISM cluster descriptions scored AUROC 0.85 (GPT-2 XL) and 0.71 (Llama).
Examples built from Qwen3-32B neuron explanations fired strongly 76% of the time, near misses 11%.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: Models above 100B parameters, and mixture-of-experts models.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V6.studies_by_size has only the keys 'not stated', '1-10B', '<1B' and '10-100B' (no >100B); versions.V6.studies_by_family lists other or not stated, GPT-2, Llama, Gemma, Pythia, GPT (OpenAI API) and Qwen, with no MoE family.

untested.what: An independent test at 10–100B, including on Qwen3-32B: audit-style (agent or expert) explanations scored by a group other than the essay's author, with recall measured on natural text the explanation does not cover.
untested.basis: counts: versions.V6.studies_by_size['10-100B'] = 1 and versions.V6.studies_by_family.Qwen = 1; the only Qwen3-32B rows are the essay's (R4, R5, R7). The essay's untested line says recall is not measured. Bills tests explanations against written examples only in automated form. In its revision experiment, GPT-4 revises each explanation using activations on 5 GPT-4-written sentences, and the explanations are scored on held-out written sentences. Revised explanations score better on both the original and augmented sets (figures only) but are often too narrow. Bills' subjects are GPT-2 only (GPT-3-series up to 6.7B for size trends), with no expert or agent audits and no recall measure on natural text.
studies: TITLE:Language models can explain neurons in language models

untested.what: Negative poles: whether explanations of a neuron's negative side predict where it fires negatively.
untested.basis: The essay's R4 condition restricts the test to explanations of the positive side; no other study in the pack separates poles. No counts key covers poles.

untested.what: A per-neuron comparison between an inspection judgement of 'one main job' and the explanation's held-out prediction score, which is the link the version's 'so ... overstates' needs.
untested.basis: Untested-parts lines of arXiv:2606.03990 (no comparison of a judged 'one job' with per-neuron prediction quality) and arXiv:2506.05774 (how much inspection overstates is not measured). No counts key covers it.

wording_issues.phrase: fail to predict where it fires
wording_issues.issue: The studies measure two different failures. Predicted firing that does not happen (false positives, low precision): Bills R9; 2309.10312 (GPT-2 XL, GPT-4 explanations scored ≥0.8) precision 0.64 overall, which split by explanation type is 0.78 for form-based (regex-checkable) explanations and 0.62 for the rest. Firing the explanation does not predict (missed firings, low recall): 2309.10312 recall 0.50, not reported by explanation type; AlexNet unit fc7.255 has recall .08 at perfect precision (1.0), the highest in that model, and its top-60 precision, a separate measure, is .97 (2007.01062); GPT-5.4 recall 0.698±0.038 on OpenCLIP ViT-B/16 neurons (2606.03990). The essay's test checks how often examples written from the explanation fire strongly (76%) and how often near misses do (11%). It does not measure recall on natural text. The statement does not say which failure it means.
also: TITLE:Language models can explain neurons in language models

wording_issues.phrase: an explanation that fits a neuron's activating examples
wording_issues.issue: Where fit to the activating examples is measured, it is partial. 2204.10965 (CLIP-Dissect; from the text, not rows), A.10: 2 evaluators rated descriptions against the 10 most highly activating images for 50 random neurons per layer, in 5 layers of ResNet-18 (Places365) and ResNet-50 (ImageNet). The average score is 0.655, descriptions are rated good for 55–80% of neurons depending on layer, and the evaluators agreed on 68.4%. App. B (MTurk, up to 200 random neurons per layer, 3 raters): mean rating 3.57 out of 5 vs 2.61 for random descriptions. A.8: 69.7% (ResNet-18) and 77.8% (ResNet-50) of neurons are above the interpretability cutoff. Its A.7 top-0.1% match is qualitative, and the verdict codes those rows cannot_determine (the premise). BERT (2104.07143): both annotators found a pattern in 20 of 25 neuron sets (80%), against 4 of 29 random sentence sets (14%) (r1, cannot_determine). In sets judged meaningful, the pattern covered a mean of 6.80 of the 10 top sentences for neurons (SD 2.37), 6.89 for random directions and 5.05 for random sentence sets; a pattern needed at least 3 examples (from the text). Other supporting studies give no measure of fit. The lw post does not measure how well the explanation fits its source excerpts and says only that it 'did not seem to add up' to the neuron's total behaviour. 2506.07985 reports only full-distribution correlation.

Most tests score automated LLM explanations or algorithmic labels, not inspection: GPT-4 in 2309.10312, Llama 3.1 70b in 2410.13928, gpt-4o-mini, Gemini 1.5 Pro, GPT-5.4, N2G, MILAN, CLIP-Dissect. The untested-parts lines of 2309.10312 and 2410.13928 say human inspection was not tested. Human-judgement evidence comes from InceptionV1 psychophysics (2010.12606) and BERT annotators. The essay's agent and author audit, the method the version targets, is tested only by the essay itself. No study scores a 'one main job' judgement as such.

No study measures by how much. The size of the failure ranges widely with the setting. At one end it is a minority: with PRISM best-of-5, 91.67% of GPT-2 XL features show positive MAD. At the other it is near chance: Llama 3.1 8b detection is 0.53 against a 0.51 random baseline in 2410.13928. The untested-parts lines of 2606.03990 and 2506.05774 both say the overstatement is not quantified.

Many tests are not on language-model MLP neurons. 2104.07143 uses BERT final-layer [CLS] basis dimensions. 2309.08600 scores learned SAE features and baseline directions (default basis, random, PCA, ICA) in the Pythia-70M residual stream, with negative activations zeroed so only the positive side is scored. The text names Pythia-70M in the Fig 8 caption, not in the Fig 9 caption that R3 comes from, and its MLP neurons appear only in Appendix C.3. 2405.20331 and other studies use vision CNN or ViT units. The essay audits neuron poles and tested only positive-side explanations; no other study separates poles.

Several supporting results are single-neuron existence cases, not rates. The lw post studies one neuron, L21 N4526 (Pearson 0.25 and −0.02). 2411.08166 shows one GPT2-small neuron with an almost 50:1 primary-to-secondary ratio. The Whisper post shows two neurons. Rates across neurons come from other studies, and they depend on layer and method.

method_sensitivity.what: In a six-layer SoLU model, N2G F1 is 0.74 (2304.12918) and 0.68 (2305.19911) in layer 0, and falls to as low as 0.42 and to 0.37–0.45 in layers 3–5. One-layer GPT-2 shows no random-only drop (8.9 vs 8.8), while L≥2 does (L=2: 1.95 vs 4.2) (2410.16443). In Gemma-2-2b (MaxAct* descriptions, 1,000 random features per layer), FADE Clarity, Responsiveness and Purity are worst at layer 12 (Purity 0.43) and best at the tuned layer 20 (Purity 0.61). Faithfulness does not follow this order (2502.16994).
also: TITLE:Language models can explain neurons in language models

method_sensitivity.factor: Scoring set (random-only vs top-and-random; activating inputs only)
method_sensitivity.what: Explanations score lower on random-only sets than on top-and-random sets. In GPT-2 at L=12 the mean interpretation score (ρ, %) is 2.67 vs 6.34 (2410.16443). In the Pythia-70M residual stream (SAE features and baseline directions, including the default basis), the text calls random-only scores significantly smaller than top-and-random scores but gives no numbers and reports no test (2309.08600). A Recall metric limited to highly activating inputs never penalises over-generic labels (0.00% Decrease Acc; 2506.05774), and its authors report that top-and-random sampling changes how Correlation behaves.
also: TITLE:Language models can explain neurons in language models

method_sensitivity.what: In CoSy, MILAN and CLIP-Dissect differ in the same layers: ResNet50 ImageNet AUC 0.44±0.23 vs 0.95±0.08 (2405.20331). Top-activation DnD scores 0.1534 against full-range LE at 0.241 on ResNet-50 (2506.07985). In SHV, the concept source moves ResNet-50 Activation Rate from 45.01% (Network Dissect) to 57.91% (CLIP-Dissect, Common Words) (2603.24953). PRISM mean vs max descriptions of GPT-2 XL give AUROC 0.65 vs 0.85 (2506.15538).

The evaluation-text generator changes PRISM scores for GPT-2 XL MLP neurons (60 random neurons in 3 layers; Table 5). For PRISM max (best of 5 descriptions), each entry gives AUROC on a 0–1 scale with its 95% CI, then the share of features with positive MAD in %. Gemini 1.5 Pro (default): 0.85 (0.78-0.91), 91.67%. Qwen3 32B: 0.58 (0.46-0.69), 58.33%. Phi-4: 0.61 (0.50-0.72), 58.33%. DeepSeek R1: 0.71 (0.61-0.80), 73.33%. PRISM mean AUROC is 0.65, 0.53, 0.54 and 0.57 in the same order; for DeepSeek R1, mean positive MAD is 57.67%. The supports verdict's 'near chance with other evaluation generators' does not fit DeepSeek R1 with PRISM max. The authors call the drops 'slightly lower' and say the method ranking is preserved (2506.15538).

method_sensitivity.factor: Activation range, threshold or dataset used for the examples
method_sensitivity.what: Descriptions match top-0.1% images but not the top 1% and 5% (2204.10965). For the 'Monarch' unit fc6.1199, false alarms are .02 at the top-60 threshold and above 99% at maximum informedness (2007.01062). Two Whisper tiny neurons sound single-phoneme at top activation but are polysemantic at lower ranges (Whisper post). BERT patterns change with the dataset the top examples come from: 2.5 patterns per neuron (2104.07143).

method_sensitivity.factor: Measure (precision vs recall, simulation score vs other measures)
method_sensitivity.what: AlexNet fc7.255 has precision .97 but recall .08 at perfect precision (2007.01062). The GPT-4 simulation score correlates −0.1 with F1 among GPT-2 XL explanations scored ≥0.8 (2309.10312). A Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct neuron scores 0.77 on simulation but near-zero Purity (2502.16994). GPT-5.4 predictions for OpenCLIP ViT-B/16 have precision 0.865±0.042 but recall 0.698±0.038 (2606.03990).

method_sensitivity.factor: Prediction task, reference type and number of examples shown
method_sensitivity.what: On InceptionV1 extreme queries, natural references give 92±2% and synthetic ones 82±4%; a single natural reference gives 73±4% (2010.12606). The occlusion task with top-activating references gives 66±3% to 67±5% (2106.12447). 2106.12447's coarse forward-simulation replication gives 84±3% for natural references (from the text). In 2606.03990, the VLM's monosemanticity judgements fall as more top-activating images are shown (no number in rows).

method_sensitivity.factor: Rater (automated vs human) and explainer/simulator pipeline
method_sensitivity.what: On ResNet-50 Layer4, the rater changes absolute scores and the order of DnD and CLIP-Dissect, but LE stays above DnD under every rater. The study names LE as the only method it tests that targets the full activation range. Automated SigLIP-simulated correlation on a 10,000-input test split: DnD 0.1534, CLIP-Dissect 0.1904, LE 0.241. Human ratings on 100 random neurons, majority vote: DnD 0.0978, CLIP-Dissect 0.0978, LE 0.1216. With BRAgg and a uniform prior: DnD 0.1011, CLIP-Dissect 0.1017, LE 0.1261 (LE>DnD p=0.0198) (2506.07985). For GPT-2 XL neuron L21 N4526, Opus 5.5 as explainer and simulator scores Pearson 0.25, using 35 examples, multi-sentence explanations and direct 0–10 simulation. GPT-4 as explainer and simulator scores −0.02. In the post's appendix (10 neurons), the Opus simulator alone did better on GPT-4's explanations, and the full Opus combination had the strongest effect. So the simulator and the recipe also contribute to the gap, not only the explainer (lw:drMv4SM2gaxk3oz3m).

method_sensitivity.factor: Examples shown to the explainer (top vs random vs quantile sampling)
method_sensitivity.what: Which activating examples the explainer sees changes scores. This was tested on SAE features, not neurons. The subjects were the 131k Gemma 2 9b residual-stream SAE features, with Llama 3.1 70b as explainer and scorer. The scoring set was fixed at 100 activating examples (10 per decile) plus 100 non-activating ones. Explanations written from top-activating examples get a fuzzing median of 0.73, against 0.76 from random sampling and 0.77 from quantile sampling. Detection medians are 0.72, 0.74 and 0.74. The authors add that scoring only on top-activating examples would hide this effect (2410.13928; Fig 2, Table A6, section F.3). These numbers come from the checker's reading of the text. The pack has no row for them, only a method-sensitivity line giving the direction.

status_amendment.public_note: We clarified that the count of studies limiting this challenge's scope was made before our checks and still includes two studies that the checks re-read as supporting the challenge, so it overstates the limits until it is recounted. The level stays at R2.
